script.title: How to Spot Fake Silver — Reel 3

segments.narration: Six at-home tests catch 99 percent of fake silver. Here are the two most buyers skip.

Pure bullion is stamped 999, meaning 99.9 percent silver. The Maple Leaf runs at 9999. Sterling silver, used in jewelry, is 925. Pre-1964 USA coins are 900 silver, called junk silver. A fake coin can carry any of these stamps. The hallmark is a starting point, not proof.

segments.text: XRF CATCHES WHAT OTHER TESTS MISS
segments.narration: Handheld XRF machines identify the full elemental composition of a coin without damage. Most coin dealers have one. Ask them to run a test on your sample before a large purchase. It's the only test that catches a tungsten core that passes everything else.
Send this to someone who is buying silver for the first time.
